articles.title: Iranian Insider Claims Kuwait Strike That Killed Two Italians Was A Ukrainian "False Flag" To Impress Trump
articles.description: Iranian Insider Claims Kuwait Strike That Killed Two Italians Was A Ukrainian "False Flag" To Impress Trump A former adviser to Iran's nuclear negotiating team is blaming Ukraine for Thursday's drone strike in Kuwait that killed two Italian defense technicians, claiming the attack was a "false flag" by Kyiv meant to show President Trump what Ukraine can do, as Tehran's diplomats denied any role and called the incident "suspicious." "It is widely believed in Iran that the attack on Kuwait was a false flag operation, likely carried out by the Ukrainian regime, because its operatives are now present across the region, including in northern Iraq and Syria," Mohammad Marandi, who advised Iran's negotiators in the talks with the US in Pakistan, wrote on X. "Ukraine aims to demonstrate its potential to Trump." Five hours later Marandi went further, tying Zelensky to Israel and putting the onus on Kuwait: "If Kuwait is sincere, it should agree to a joint investigation." The Revolutionary Guards-affiliated Fars news agency pushed the same line, quoting an unnamed security source who claimed Ukrainian operatives had deployed thousands of drones and other unmanned aircraft across several Middle Eastern countries, including Iraq's Kurdistan region. Iran's official response stopped short of naming Kyiv. Its embassy in Rome "categorically" rejected the allegation that Iran was behind the attack and warned of "'false flag' activities and operations aimed at expanding the scope of the conflict," including "drawing Europe into the crisis." Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he had called his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts to offer condolences, and that "the incident is suspicious and looks like a precooked recipe for war." Tehran, he added, stands "ready to cooperate with Kuwait and Italy to determine the cause of the incident." Kuwait's Defense Ministry said debris from intercepted Iranian drones struck a military facility on Thursday, wounding four people, among them a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national. The two Italians later died of their injuries. As we reported, the attack was big enough to divert commercial air traffic in the area. Italy's Foreign Ministry said the men were civilian technicians for Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian arm of the German arms maker, doing maintenance on antennas for the Skyguard air defense system used by Kuwait's armed forces. ANSA named them as Antonio Saccoccio, 65, of Formia, and Emanuele Lo Russo, 36, of Rome. Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said Rome would lodge a complaint with Iran's embassy. Saudi Arabia held Tehran responsible and demanded an immediate halt to its attacks, Bahrain asked the UN Security Council to hold Iran to account, and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called for more pressure on Tehran, saying Gulf security "is a matter of security for us all." The Ukrainian angle rests on a deployment Kyiv has advertised itself. Zelensky has confirmed some 200 Ukrainian drone operatives are in the Middle East, with teams in Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE and Saudi Arabia helping shoot down Iranian Shaheds, some of them at Washington's request. "Ukraine has the greatest experience in the world in countering attack drones," he said in March. In July, after Iraq's national security adviser said people working for Ukraine had bombed Iraqi government facilities, Ukraine's Foreign Ministry rejected "the unfounded and unsubstantiated allegations" and said they matched Russian propaganda. Kuwait, a key US ally, has come under repeated Iranian fire since the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran on Feb. 28. Earlier this month, Iran hit US bases in Kuwait after the Pentagon struck Qeshm Island, and this time Tehran is asking Kuwait and Italy to investigate with it. Tyler Durden Fri, 11/27/2026 - 23:00

articles.title: Gadi Eisenkot vows to form new Israeli Government within eight days, accuses Likud of stalling talks
articles.description: Jerusalem: Israeli opposition bloc leader Gadi Eisenkot said that he intends to form a new government within the eight days remaining in his mandate, accusing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party of conducting unity negotiations without any genuine intention of reaching an agreement. In a social media post, Eisenkot said that the two sides had held five meetings over two weeks, but Likud allegedly refused to make concrete proposals or compromise on key issues, including removing far-right parties from the government, establishing a state commission of inquiry into the October 7, 2023 attack, and passing legislation requiring broader military service. Eisenkot accused Likud of deliberately delaying negotiations to divide the opposition and force another election. He said his bloc had offered significant compromises on judicial reform and the proposed inquiry, Xinhua news agency reported. In response, Likud accused Eisenkot of conducting a political double game, claiming he was already assembling an alternative coalition, distributing ministerial portfolios and preparing to rely on Arab parties, which Likud described as supporters of terrorism. Meanwhile, former prime minister Naftali Bennett, leader of Israel's opposition faction Together, said he prefers forming a national unity government, adding that if this proves impossible, the bloc will move forward with a less desirable alternative. Earlier this month, Netanyahu called for the formation of a national unity government, asserting that the country must remain united in the face of what he described as a growing threat from Iran. Speaking after the first session of Israel's newly elected parliament, Netanyahu warned that the country could soon come under intense international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran and the continuation of its current regime, which he accused of posing an existential threat to Israel. "In the very near future, we're going to be confronted by international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran and the preservation of this terror regime that seeks to annihilate us," Netanyahu said. (IANS)
